Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: With China set to relax their one-child policy, what kind of effect will this have on their population, their consumption of the world's resources and their economy over the next 50 years?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine China is a big family. For a long time, this family could only have one child per family. Now, they are going to let families have more children.

**What happens to the family (population)?**  
More babies will be born! So, the big family (China) will start to have more people, just like if every family in your neighborhood had more kids.

**What happens to the toys and snacks (resources)?**  
If there are more kids, they will all want toys, food, and other things. This means China will need more of everything—like food, water, and energy. They might use up more of the world’s toys and snacks than before.

**What happens to the piggy bank (economy)?**  
More kids mean more people who can buy things and work when they grow up. This can help the piggy bank (economy) get bigger. But at first, when the kids are little, the family (government) might need to spend more money to take care of them, like buying more food and school supplies.

**In 50 years?**  
If there are more people, China might become even richer because more people can work and buy things. But they will also need to make sure there are enough resources for everyone and take care of the environment.

So, letting families have more children will make China’s family bigger, use more stuff, and maybe help the economy grow—but it will also bring some new challenges!
